---
title: "Health, Safety, Fieldwork, Biospecimens, and Remote Work"
---

This chapter replaces the original manual's COVID-specific section with a broader, durable policy covering the range of settings our hybrid group works in: remote and home offices, fieldwork and community sites, any biospecimen handling, and shared facilities. It also retains a flexible public-health protocol for when one is needed.

## General principle

> **Your health and safety come first.** No deadline, dataset, or deliverable is worth your wellbeing. Tell the PI or your mentor about any health or safety concern — including allergies or conditions that affect your work — so we can support you.

## Remote and hybrid work

Most of our work is computational and can be done remotely. To make remote work healthy and effective:

- **Ergonomics matter.** Set up a workspace that protects your eyes, wrists, and back; take regular breaks.
- **Sustainable hours.** We do not measure worth by hours online. Get the work done well; protect rest and boundaries (@sec-funding covers wellbeing and burnout prevention more fully).
- **Availability, not surveillance.** Keep your availability current so work is planned realistically; we trust members to manage their time. (We do **not** use geo-location time-tracking; that practice from the wet-lab era is retired.)
- **Security travels with you.** Remote work follows the same data-governance rules (@sec-data-governance): no restricted data on personal devices or unsecured networks; analyze controlled data only in approved environments.
- **Stay connected.** Remote members are deliberately included in meetings, decisions, authorship, and the social life of the group (@sec-belonging).

## Fieldwork and community sites

When work happens in communities, partner clinics, or field settings:

- **Plan and brief first.** Confirm site contacts, logistics, consent procedures, and an emergency plan before going.
- **Respect community partners.** We are guests; follow partner site rules and cultural norms. Communities are collaborators, not subjects.
- **Never photograph or record research participants** (@sec-data-governance). Capture only what consent and IRB allow.
- **Travel safely.** Follow institutional travel and safety policies; don't work alone in unfamiliar settings without a check-in plan.
- **Protect data in transit.** Field-collected data follows the same security and de-identification rules from the moment it's captured.

## Biospecimens (when applicable)

If a project involves biological specimens (human blood, tissue, or environmental bioaerosol samples):

- Complete required bloodborne-pathogen and biosafety training and maintain relevant vaccinations (e.g., Hepatitis B) per institutional policy when handling human blood/fluids.
- Follow the biosafety level, PPE, and handling procedures for the facility and protocol.
- Label, store, log, and chain-of-custody specimens per the protocol; never improvise. Inventory and location of record live in **Aliquary** (@sec-aliquary).
- Dispose of biological and chemical waste per institutional and regulatory rules.
- Wear appropriate PPE and follow facility dress/safety codes when in a lab space.

::: {.callout-note}
## Placeholder: facility-specific safety rules
Exact biosafety levels, PPE requirements, vaccination/clearance rules, waste procedures, and emergency contacts depend on the specific facility and institution. These **must be confirmed locally** before any wet-lab or biospecimen work and recorded in the project's operating manual.
:::

## Sample inventory with Aliquary {#sec-aliquary}

When a project holds physical samples — human biospecimens, environmental bioaerosols, or other aliquoted materials — **[Aliquary](https://www.aliquary.com)** is our **sample-inventory system of record**. Spreadsheets and ad-hoc freezer lists are not an inventory.

Aliquary is how we:

- **Register** samples (with the metadata the project requires).
- **Map** freezers, racks, and boxes so every vial has a known home.
- **Look up** anything by barcode when someone needs it at the bench.
- **Track** aliquots and freeze–thaw cycles so usage history is auditable.

### Workflow: register → locate → track → export

1. **Register.** Create the sample record in Aliquary when the material enters inventory — before it goes into a box.
2. **Locate.** Assign (and keep current) freezer / rack / box / position; use barcode lookup to find it again.
3. **Track.** Record aliquoting and freeze–thaw events as they happen; do not backfill from memory.
4. **Export.** When a project archives, migrates, or ends, export the inventory so we retain a complete record with **no lock-in**.

Governance for what may be stored in Aliquary (de-identified only, tenant isolation, audit trail, export) is in @sec-aliquary-governance. Account access is provisioned at onboarding and revoked at offboarding (@sec-onboarding).

::: {.callout-note}

## Public-health and infectious-disease protocol (flexible)

Rather than a single pandemic-specific section, we keep a **scalable protocol** that activates when public-health conditions require it (a respiratory illness surge, a new advisory, fieldwork in an outbreak area):

- Follow current institutional, local, state, and federal guidance — that guidance, not this manual, is authoritative and current.
- The PI may activate measures proportionate to the situation: remote-first work, masking, distancing, capacity limits in shared spaces, testing, or pausing in-person activity.
- **Stay home when sick**; we would always rather you rest than risk others. Sickness is never penalized.
- For fieldwork during an active outbreak, add a site-specific risk assessment to the project operating manual.

## Reporting incidents

Report any injury, exposure, near-miss, safety concern, or health-and-safety question to the PI promptly. Reporting is expected and never penalized — early reporting keeps everyone safe.
